C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW.Summary: Fix the retirement clamp so that retiring content opens a write window instead of erasing it: on a --retire that moves at least one element, the findings ceiling is min(previous ceiling, pre-move base plus headroom), not min(previous ceiling, post-move base plus headroom). The move therefore opens a window of retired lines plus headroom that the next flush consumes and the following --retire closes. The findings genre only: rulings keeps the post-move timing with the clamp now unconditional, registry and index keep their formulas. Remove the spent one-time rulings exception (isFirstRulingsRewrite) shipped by C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY, whose stop condition is content-derived and can re-fire by coincidence, and replace it with a validator-asserted provenance ceiling on the rulings genre so the 1883 correction stays pinned and any later raise is constructively a hand edit. Pays F183 (staged buffer). Binding live rulings D28, D28.1, D30; D31 layers. Overturns the findings half of C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's ceiling ruling, with the original argument answered in Constraints. No graph module is written; src/ is not edited. Name provisional, awaiting the maintainer's charter.
C-RETIREMENT-WINDOW.Problem:
The retirement clamp is re-derived from the post-move footprint at every --retire, so retiring content removes an equal amount of ceiling. Shipped code: persistSnapshot (scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:858) computes ceiling as min(previous.ceiling, base + headroom) and retireRecord (:933) passes the post-move line count as base (:1067-1081). Under D28.1 the ceiling is the backstop and eligibility the enforcement, but the backstop as shrink-to-fit makes retirement unable to create room: headroom is the only room there will ever be, permanently. Staged F183 (buffer, not record) measured this: the findings breach of the staged buffer was the same size before and after C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's move of 15 eligible findings. The record cannot accept the D30-staged buffer (.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md) until the window mechanism ships; the genres are entangled with citations in both directions, so no partial flush exists (staged F183, re-measured for this spec in Assumptions).
C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY corrected the rulings multiplier 2 to 7 and shipped a read-time predicate (isFirstRulingsRewrite, scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:504) that let the rulings ceiling correct itself exactly once by disabling the clamp on the first ruling rewrite whose persisted shape still matched the uncorrected sizing. It fired in that bundle (git show of the move in Assumptions) and its intended purpose is exhausted: the current rulings snapshot is exactly what the corrected formula produces. But its stop condition is not structural. When a clamped rewrite binds, the persisted headroom becomes previousCeiling minus base (persistSnapshot :858-868), an arbitrary integer; if that integer later equals 2 times the then-live median while the formula term exceeds the persisted ceiling, the predicate fires again and raises the ceiling as an accident of arithmetic -- a raise no human decided, the act D28.1 made non-negotiable. A spend-once predicate that can re-fire on content coincidence is not spent; this bundle removes it and preserves the correction's provenance as a checked invariant instead of a comment.
The headroom constant H stays sourced in tracked repository space (7 times the median live element line count, :1065). It must never be a function of the untracked staged buffer: a ceiling derived from a .gitignored file is unreproducible from a fresh clone and greenable by appending to local state (D28.1, rejected explicitly). Staged F182's median-rounding defect is adjacent and stays with its owner; this bundle does not re-size H.

Goals.Goal: The findings retirement window. After a --retire that moved at least one element, persist on the findings live root: base = the post-move line count of findings.xml; ceiling = min(previously persisted ceiling, Base_live + H), where Base_live is the pre-retirement line count of findings.xml as read on entry and H = 7 times the median line count of the live Finding elements after the move (the shipped derivation (:1065), population unchanged); headroom = ceiling - base, so the three attributes remain a consistent snapshot and headroom reads as the open window. The move opens Delta_retired + H; the next flush consumes it; the following --retire closes it back toward H. With Delta_retired = 0 -- a move of other genres while findings is unchanged -- the min yields a window of exactly H when the snapshot sits at base + H (its steady state), and consumes the window exactly as growth lands. The min is required, not optional: without it the ceiling rises whenever growth outpaces the previous retirement, which is a ratchet upward and inverts the invariant (D28.1).

Remove the spent one-time rulings exception. Delete isFirstRulingsRewrite and the discriminator branch (:947-953, :1071-1073): the rulings clamp becomes unconditional, which is the current rulings behaviour for every intended future state -- the exception's purpose ended with the correction it shipped. The six references to the predicate in the retirement test file are replaced by clamp-always fixtures.

Provenance for the corrected rulings ceiling, validator-asserted rather than comment-carried. A named constant in scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts carries the ceiling value that C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's one-time correction persisted (the historical exception belongs to that bundle, not to C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2, which set the sizing it corrected); the non-mutating validate run errors when the rulings live root persists a ceiling above it. Under the clamp an upward move has no in-product producer, so a larger value is constructively a hand edit. The failure message names the provenance and says raising the persisted value is not the remedy; it never names a config key (D28.1). A future bundle that legitimately re-sizes rulings amends the constant, with its own citation, inside its own spec.

Observable trigger, confirmed and kept. Every write of base / headroom / ceiling happens inside an argv the engine itself executes: retireRecord (:933, the four withRootSnapshot calls at :1067-1081, after the movedCount === 0 early return at :1024) or the one-shot split (splitFrozenRecord :578, which refuses a stub at :583). --stamp-paid-by (:909) writes PaidBy children only. Validation is read-only and is the validate:ci member (package.json:72, :77). The window's clamp inputs are the pre-move bytes of findings.xml and the post-move live medians, both measured at the event, plus the persisted previous ceiling; no step depends on an operator gesture the system cannot observe.

No new transition machinery. The findings ratchet ships with no one-time predicate, kind= marker, or self-erasing branch: the cutover is continuous at the persisted state (arithmetic in Assumptions), and the only reads of persisted base and headroom today are the exception being deleted and the snapshot rewrite itself; validation compares occupancy to the persisted ceiling only (checkCeilingValue, :1267). Do not reinvent an exception mechanism this change does not need.

Carried decisions -- implemented, not relitigated. (1) The formula is single-invocation: Base_k = Base_live - Delta_retired and Ceiling_k = min(Ceiling_(k-1), Base_live + H) at one --retire event; there is no lagged pass. (2) The min is required. (3) The findings genre only: rulings keeps the post-move timing (below), and the registry / index genres keep their formulas entirely. (4) H stays a constant derived in tracked repository space, never a function of the staged buffer or any untracked state (D28.1: the rejected shape makes the CI criterion unreproducible from a fresh clone and greenable by appending to a .gitignored file). The findings ceiling ruling, normative. On entry to the snapshot rewrite, capture Base_live as the newline count of findings.xml as read, before any spans are removed. After the move: base = post-move line count; H = 7 times the median post-move live Finding element line count via the shipped median (:118) and line-count path; ceiling = min(previous persisted ceiling, Base_live + H); headroom = ceiling - base. This overturns the findings half of C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's ceiling ruling (CLAUDE.md rule 9, stated): that bundle's argument for the clamp was that a formula recompute across its multiplier fix must not raise the rulings ceiling past the correction, and its findings half -- min over the post-move base -- was applied without a findings-specific argument. The min, which was the load-bearing half of that ruling, is kept; what changes is the base the second term measures, which the original Constraint derived as live size at that moment and which staged F183 measured as erasing the room retirement creates. The original argument's counterweight -- no raise without a decision -- survives intact under the pre-move term. The ceiling failure message continues to name --retire / move to the retired sibling and says raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy; it never names a config key or a multiplier. Do not pin a scalar count of a record file into this Constraint (D30); the measured occupancy is in Assumptions.

Snapshot consistency across genres. Every live root persists a triple with headroom = ceiling - base after a rewrite. For rulings, registry, and index this is behaviourally the shipped rule -- when the formula term sets the ceiling, ceiling - base is exactly the computed headroom, and when the clamp binds the shipped code already persists ceiling - base (:866). For findings it is the same statement and yields headroom = Delta_retired + H when the formula term sets the ceiling. The current production record satisfies base + headroom = ceiling on all four live roots (Assumptions), so this codifies the existing invariant, it does not introduce a new state shape.

The exception removal, with the reason removal beats dormancy. isFirstRulingsRewrite (:504-513), the discriminator computation (:947-953), and the !discriminator clamp branch (:1071-1073) are deleted; the rulings persistSnapshot call passes clamp = true always. Dormant is not safe: the predicate reads persisted headroom at every rewrite, the clamped-rewrite rule persists headroom = previousCeiling - base, and that value equals 2 times a future live median only by coincidence -- but if it does, at a moment when the formula term exceeds the persisted ceiling, the clamp is disabled and the ceiling rises with no ratified decision. D28.1 forbids exactly that act, so the mechanism is removed rather than left armed. The retirement test file's split-shape probes of the first-rewrite behaviour are replaced by fixtures proving a split-shaped (uncorrected-sizing) ruling file keeps its previous ceiling under a --retire whose 7-times formula term exceeds it -- the discriminating direction against the deleted behaviour. Archived C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY and its acceptance criteria are immutable history: this bundle supersedes the engine, not that bundle's record.

The provenance invariant. The non-mutating validate path gains one check: the rulings live root's persisted ceiling must not exceed the named constant carrying the ceiling C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY persisted at its move. The constant carries the number; its comment carries only the citation (bundle name and move commit), so the number cannot drift from a paraphrase. The error's message says: the persisted rulings ceiling exceeds the value C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's one-time correction persisted; no shipped operation raises it; restore from git; raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy. Fixture tests plant both directions: at the constant, validation passes; one above it, validation exits non-zero with the provenance message. This check reads the persisted attribute; it does not recompute occupancy and adds no scalar count of a record file to any Constraint (D30).

No one-time transition for the findings ratchet. Explicitly: this change needs no discriminator. The new formula is continuous at the persisted state -- at Delta_retired = 0 on the current snapshot it persists min of the current ceiling and the current base plus the current shipped headroom, which is the current ceiling (Assumptions). Nothing re-reads persisted base or headroom for behaviour once the exception is gone. No kind= attribute, no marker element, no self-erasing branch ships. If a plan author is tempted to mirror the deleted predicate for findings, this Constraint is the refusal.

Registry and index keep the current timing, and the asymmetry is correct. Index: a move flips an Entry's layer attribute in place and removes zero lines, so its pre- and post-move bases coincide and the two timings are identical there -- applying the new timing would be a no-op. Registry: base is a count of live rows, growth and retirement are denominated in the same unit, and they balance one-for-one over a bundle's life -- a charter adds one row and that bundle's archive event later removes one -- so the genre cannot accumulate retired-more-than- arrived the way findings does, where one bundle can pay arbitrarily many entries against a single registry row. Pressure measured at this spec's commit is absent (Assumptions). If registry pressure is ever measured, the findings template now exists; growing this bundle to a genre with no measured defect is refused (D11's mirror: no scope without a dependency).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-WINDOW-FORMULA:
A fixture --retire that moves at least one finding after the live findings file was grown by hand persists ceiling equal to the previously persisted ceiling when Base_live + H meets or exceeds it, base equal to the post-move line count, and headroom equal to ceiling minus base -- the window opened is Delta_retired + H minus the growth the fixture applied. The same fixture under the shipped post-move term would persist a smaller ceiling, so the assertion discriminates the formula, and a no-min recompute that raises the ceiling also fails it. A fixture whose findings content was hand-shrunk below the snapshot without a move persists ceiling = Base_live + H, proving the min is not decorative. After any successful move, every live root's persisted triple satisfies base + headroom = ceiling. Failure: the second term of the min reads the post-move line count; the ceiling ever rises; headroom desynchronises from ceiling minus base; registry or index gains the pre-move term.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXCEPTION-REMOVED:
isFirstRulingsRewrite, the discriminator, and the rulings clamp branch are absent from scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts and from the test file's imports. A fixture in the split-time (uncorrected-sizing) shape under a --retire whose 7-times formula term exceeds the persisted ceiling keeps the previous ceiling; the deleted engine persisted the larger formula value on that shape, so the probe discriminates the removal. A second --retire on that fixture still never raises. Failure: the engine retains a branch that can disable the rulings clamp; the fixture suite cannot tell removal from dormancy.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-PROVENANCE-CEILING:
The non-mutating validate run errors when the rulings live root persists a ceiling above the named constant carrying the value C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's one-time correction persisted, with a message stating the provenance, that no shipped operation raises it, and that raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy. Fixture probes run both directions: at the constant passes, one above errors. Production validation stays green, as measured at this spec's commit (Assumptions). Failure: the number exists only in prose or a comment and no check compares against it; the message names a config key or a multiplier.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NOOP-RETIRE:
A --retire with nothing eligible exits 0 and writes no attribute and no byte: fixture probe plus, at close, bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --retire on the production record followed by git diff --exit-code over the record subtree, empty. Failure: a no-op --retire rewrites a ceiling, or the engine requires an operator gesture outside the argv it executes.
